reason: The bearing frames appear to support the rotating crankshaft on the mechanism base.
expectation: The frames will attach to the base to support the crankshaft.

alternatives.reason: The cam also needs to turn with the shaft, but the base seems a practical starting point.

effect: The bearing frames are installed, so the base is ready for the shaft assembly.
reason: The off-centre cam needs to rotate with the crankshaft to lift the follower.
expectation: The cam will attach to the crankshaft.

alternatives.reason: I could install the shaft first, but attaching the cam beforehand seems practical.

effect: The cam has no available combination yet, so it may need the shaft to be installed first.
reaction: The assembly order was less flexible than I expected.
reason: The installed bearings should support the crankshaft.
expectation: The crankshaft will fit into the bearings.

effect: The crankshaft is installed, so I can try fitting the cam to it now.
reaction: The required order makes more sense now.
reason: The cam should turn with the installed crankshaft and provide the lifting motion.
expectation: The cam will attach to the crankshaft.

effect: The cam is installed, and its off-centre shape will make its edge rise and fall as the shaft turns.
reaction: Seeing why an off-centre disc matters is satisfying.
reason: The follower guide should keep the rod moving in line above the cam.
expectation: The guide will attach to the mechanism, ready to hold the follower rod.

alternatives.reason: The rod might fit directly, but it seems likely to need its guide first.

effect: The follower rod and guide assemble together before being fitted to the mechanism.
reaction: The automatic assembly clarified the order.
reason: The guided follower should sit against the cam so the turning disc can move it.
expectation: The guided follower will attach to the cam mechanism.

effect: The guided follower is installed above the cam; the spring and handle remain to complete the mechanism.
reaction: The parts are coming together as expected.
reason: The light spring should keep the follower against the cam as it rises and falls.
expectation: The spring will attach to the follower mechanism.

alternatives.reason: The handle will be needed to turn the shaft, but the follower may need its spring first.

effect: The spring is fitted, and the result suggests testing both with and without its pull.
reaction: I am curious how the spring changes the follower’s motion.
reason: The handle is needed to turn the crank and test the lifter.
expectation: The handle will attach so the crank can be turned and the follower tested.

effect: The handle completed the lifter, and testing showed that the spring keeps the follower against the cam as it falls.
reaction: The comparison made the spring’s purpose clear and was satisfying to see.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the handle and comparing the follower with and without the spring made the mechanism’s motion understandable, rather than just assembling parts.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to attach the cam to the loose crankshaft was unproductive; the required assembly order was not apparent beforehand.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the follower could sometimes hang without the spring’s pull, even though the cam itself falls away.

arbitrary.text: The cam’s refusal to combine with the loose shaft felt somewhat arbitrary, though installing the shaft first was a plausible construction order.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: learning how the cam and spring work was worthwhile, and I am curious how the lifter will make the dragon wave.
